catalog_quote: Tobian is weight-sensitive and seems to be following the hypothesis about the Pulo Annian pattern (Regh, 1993: 32), with stress assignment (intensity) being mora sensitive. Primary stress is assigned on the penultimate (from left to right) mora of the prosodic word. For example, in fioŋo-ri, story-of (Figure 19 and Table 7), a quadrimoraic prosodic word, fi/o/ŋo/ri, it is the penultimate mora ŋ[o]=73.32 dB that presents the highest intensity, while secondary stress is assigned on the preceding mora, fi[o]=72.82 dB. ... As mentioned before, all sonorant consonants can be assigned a mora. However, there are certain restrictions. • In disyllabic words ending with sonorant codas if the penultimate syllable is heavy, (usually a diphthong) it is the second mora of that syllable that is stressed instead of the penultimate mora of the prosodic word (Figures 20-22 and Tables 8-10). new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the penultimate mora of the prosodic word, counting moras on vowels (long vowels/diphthongs = two moras) and on sonorant coda consonants; so a heavy penultimate syllable attracts stress to its second mora and a final sonorant coda counts as the last mora. In practice this is penultimate-mora (moraic-trochee-like, right-edge) stress; on the syllable level it typically surfaces as penultimate-syllable stress (as the 2022 report states), but shifts within heavy syllables and with sonorant codas.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Only one measured example (fioŋo-ri: secondary intensity peak on the mora preceding the primary, p. 37). Conclusion p. 68: 'no investigation of secondary stress is presented, although it is hypothesized that it occurs on preceding moras in trimoraic feet as is characteristic of Micronesian languages (Kennedy, 2003: 35) and on final moras in disyllabic words, that is the same syllables that exhibit high pitch.'
new_statements.exceptions: pp. 38-43 (bulleted restrictions): (i) in disyllabic words ending in a sonorant coda whose penultimate syllable is heavy (usually a diphthong), it is the second mora of that heavy syllable that is stressed rather than the penultimate mora of the prosodic word; (ii) an utterance-final disyllable stresses the penultimate mora even when the penult is light; (iii) a non-final disyllable with a light penult stresses the penultimate mora (usually a mid vowel) and the sonorant coda counts as the final mora. Uncertainty whether geminates other than [m:] carry a mora (p. 34). p. 17: Capell 1969 and van den Berg 2014 contain no prosody information.
new_statements.domain_note: Prosodic word in connected speech: the analysis is instrumental (Praat intensity in dB and F0 in Hz) on archived ELAR conversation/story recordings (Black & Black collection) plus 2020 recordings with two speakers; not citation forms. Stress = intensity peak; pitch is treated separately and is syllable-based (penultimate syllable in trisyllables, final syllable in non-final disyllables, antepenult in four-syllable feet; pp. 44-50). Supporting first-hand statement, same authors: Vita, Pedro & Marino 2022: 5 'Tobian stresses the penultimate syllable, thus in bimoraic words the first syllable or mora is usually stressed'.
new_statements.identity_note: Vita 2020 describes Ramari Hatohobei = Tobian (tobi1238, ISO tox), the language of Hatohobei (Tobi) Island, Hatohobei State, Palau, from speakers now living mainly in Echang/Koror; Glottolog lists no dialects. Sister language Sonsorolese (Ramari Dongosaro, sons1242) is treated separately by the same author (Vita & Pedro 2021, no stress rule). The 'Pulo Annian pattern' Vita invokes is Rehg 1993's hypothesis for Pulo Anna (pulo1240 per Vita), applied by her to Tobian.

sources.note: p. 5: 'Tobian stresses the penultimate syllable, thus in bimoraic words the first syllable or mora is usually stressed.. due to weight sensitivity. When it is not stressed, usually in trimoraic or quadrimoraic feet, then it turns back to the low /ɐ/.' p. 6: with suffix -i a bimoraic word becomes trimoraic and 'the stress falls in the second syllable [xɐsəʝi:]'. p. 11: argues Tobian has stress-dependent vowel harmony (preliminary).
